title: Latex unclosed dollar
statement: How many two-digit positive integers have a tens digit equal to $9 times the units digit?
hints: Name the units digit, since the tens digit depends on it.
Use the place value of each digit to list the options: the tens digit is at most $9$, which limits the units digit.
solution: Let the units digit be $u$, with $u \ge 1$. The tens digit is $3u$, which must be at most $9$, so $u \in \{1, 2, 3\}$. This gives $31$, $62$ and $93$, so there are $3$ such numbers.
check_program: print(sum(1 for n in range(10, 100) if n % 10 != 0 and n // 10 == 3 * (n % 10)))
